units.subject: Mathematics
units.title: Counting to 100
units.caps: CAPS Grade 1 Mathematics: Numbers, Operations and Relationships (count forwards and backwards in 1s from any number 0 to 100; skip count in 2s, 5s and 10s; number before and after)
units.intention: Today I am practising counting on, counting back and counting in tens.
units.prompt: How did you find the number that comes next?

lesson.say: When we count on, we start at any number and keep going. Twenty-seven, twenty-eight, twenty-nine, thirty.
lesson.html:
27→28→29→30

Start at any number and count on, one more each time.

lesson.say: The number before 40 is 39. The number after 40 is 41.
lesson.html:
39→40→41

Before means one less. After means one more.

lesson.say: We can count in tens. Ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty. It is faster than counting in ones.
lesson.html:
🔟 🔟 🔟 🔟 🔟

10→20→30→40→50

Counting in tens is quick: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50.

questions.q: What number comes after 34?
questions.html: 32→33→34→?
questions.explain: 35 comes after 34.

questions.q: What number comes before 70?
questions.html: ?→70→71
questions.explain: 69 comes before 70.

questions.q: Count in tens: 10, 20, 30, what comes next?
Count in fives: 5, 10, 15, what comes next?
Count back: 18, 17, 16, what comes next?
hints: Counting back means one less each time.

questions.q: Put the numbers in order, smallest first.

units.parent: Your child counted on and back, found numbers before and after, and counted in 5s and 10s.
units.teacher: Shows counting forwards and backwards within 100, before and after, and skip counting in 5s and 10s.
units.done: You can count on, count back and count in tens.

units.subject: Mathematics
units.title: Adding and taking away to 20
units.caps: CAPS Grade 1 Mathematics: Numbers, Operations and Relationships (add and subtract to 20; number bonds to 10; solve word problems in context)
units.intention: Today I am practising adding and taking away with numbers up to 20.
units.prompt: Did you count on or count back?

lesson.say: Adding means putting groups together. Six marbles and three marbles make nine marbles.
lesson.html:
🔵 🔵 🔵 🔵 🔵 🔵 ➕ 🔵 🔵 🔵

6 + 3 = 9. Start at 6 and count on 3: 7, 8, 9.

lesson.say: Taking away means some go. Twelve birds sit on a fence and four fly away. Eight are left.
lesson.html:
🐦 🐦 🐦 🐦 🐦 🐦 🐦 🐦 🕊️ 🕊️ 🕊️ 🕊️

12 − 4 = 8. Start at 12 and count back 4: 11, 10, 9, 8.

lesson.say: Pairs that make ten are called number bonds. Seven and three make ten. Six and four make ten.
lesson.html:
1 + 9→2 + 8→3 + 7→4 + 6→5 + 5

These pairs all make 10. Knowing them helps you add fast.

example.q: Thandi has 9 sweets. Her gogo gives her 5 more. How many does she have now?

questions.q: What is 8 plus 4?
questions.html: 🍎 🍎 🍎 🍎 🍎 🍎 🍎 🍎 ➕ 🍎 🍎 🍎 🍎

questions.q: What is 15 take away 3?
Which number makes 10 with 7?
There are 11 children on the bus. 5 get off. How many are still on the bus?
questions.explain: 11 − 5 = 6 children.

questions.q: Lebo has 10 crayons and finds 6 more. How many does she have now?
questions.explain: 10 + 6 = 16 crayons.

questions.q: Sort the sums. Which make 10 and which do not?
questions.explain: 6 + 4 and 2 + 8 make 10. The others make 9.

units.parent: Your child added and subtracted with numbers to 20 and practised pairs that make 10.
units.teacher: Shows addition and subtraction to 20 using counting on and back, number bonds to 10 and word problems.
units.done: You can add and take away with numbers up to 20.

units.subject: Mathematics
units.title: Sharing and grouping
units.topic: Equal sharing, grouping and repeated addition
units.caps: CAPS Grade 1 Mathematics: Numbers, Operations and Relationships (repeated addition to 20; equal sharing and grouping to 20, including remainders)
units.intention: Today I am practising sharing things fairly and making equal groups.
units.prompt: How did you make the groups fair?

lesson.say: Sharing fairly means everyone gets the same. Six oranges shared between two children. Each child gets three.
lesson.html:
🧒 🍊🍊🍊   👧 🍊🍊🍊

6 shared between 2 is 3 each. Everyone gets the same.

lesson.say: We can put things into equal groups. Ten eggs in groups of two make five groups.
lesson.html:
🥚🥚 🥚🥚 🥚🥚 🥚🥚 🥚🥚

10 in groups of 2 makes 5 groups.

lesson.say: Sometimes some are left over. Seven sweets shared between two children is three each, with one left over.
lesson.html:
🧒 🍬🍬🍬   👧 🍬🍬🍬   ➕ 🍬

7 shared between 2 is 3 each, and 1 left over. The one left over is the remainder.

example.q: Share 12 biscuits between 3 friends. How many does each friend get?
steps: Give one biscuit to each friend, again and again.
Keep going until there are none left.

questions.q: Share 8 apples between 2 children. How many does each child get?
hints: Give one to each child at a time.
Keep going until all are given.
questions.explain: 8 shared between 2 is 4 each.

questions.q: How many groups of 5 can you make with 15 marbles?
questions.explain: 15 makes 3 groups of 5.

questions.q: What is 4 plus 4 plus 4?
hints: Add the 4s one at a time.

questions.q: Share 9 pencils between 2 children. How many are left over?
questions.explain: Each child gets 4, and 1 pencil is left over.

questions.q: Which is a fair share?
questions.explain: 3 and 3 is fair because each child gets the same.

units.parent: Your child shared things fairly, made equal groups and found what was left over.
units.teacher: Shows equal sharing and grouping to 20, repeated addition and remainders.
units.done: Fair sharing means everyone gets the same amount.

units.subject: Mathematics
units.title: Rands and cents
units.caps: CAPS Grade 1 Mathematics: Measurement and Numbers (recognise South African coins and notes; solve money problems with totals and change to R20)
units.intention: Today I am learning our coins and notes and adding up money.
units.prompt: How did you work out the total?

lesson.say: South Africa has coins for 10 cents, 20 cents, 50 cents, 1 rand, 2 rand and 5 rand.
lesson.html:
10c→20c→50c→R1→R2→R5

c means cents. R means rand. 100 cents make R1.

lesson.say: Notes are paper money. The smallest notes are 10 rand and 20 rand.
lesson.html:
💵 💵

R10→R20

Notes are worth more than most coins.

lesson.say: A R5 coin and a R2 coin make R7. We add rands the same way we add numbers.
lesson.html:
R5→+→R2→=→R7

Add money just like numbers: 5 + 2 = 7, so R7.

example.q: A juice costs R6. You pay with a R10 note. How much change do you get?
steps: Change is what is left after you pay.

questions.q: Which is the biggest amount?
questions.explain: R5 is more than R2 and R1.

questions.q: R2 and R2 and R1. How much is that?
A pencil costs R3. You pay R5. How much change?
questions.explain: R5 − R3 = R2 change.

questions.q: You buy an apple for R4 and a bun for R7. How much do you pay?
Sort into coins and notes.
questions.explain: 50c and R5 are coins. R10 and R20 are notes.

units.parent: Your child learned South African coins and notes and added up small amounts of money.
units.teacher: Shows recognition of SA coins and notes and solving totals and change to R20.
units.done: You know our coins and notes and can add up money.

units.subject: English Home Language
units.title: Word families
units.caps: CAPS Grade 1 English Home Language: Phonics (letter-sound relationships of single letters; build word families such as -at, -ig, -op, -un)
units.intention: Today I am building words that belong to the same family.
units.prompt: Which part of the words stayed the same?

lesson.say: Every letter has a sound. C, a, t. Put the sounds together and you get cat.
lesson.html:
c→a→t

🐱

Say each sound, then blend them together: c-a-t, cat.

lesson.say: Cat, hat, mat and sat all end with a t. They belong to the a t family.
lesson.html:
c-at→h-at→m-at→s-at

Words in a family end the same way. Only the first sound changes.

lesson.say: Pig, big and dig are in the i g family. Sun, run and fun are in the u n family.
lesson.html:
p-ig→b-ig→d-ig
s-un→r-un→f-un

Change the first sound to make a new word.

example.q: Change the first sound of hop to t. What word do you make?
steps: Take away h and put t: t, o, p.

questions.q: Which word is in the same family as cat?
hints: Which word ends with a t?
questions.explain: Cat and hat both end with -at.

questions.q: Which word is in the same family as pig?
questions.explain: Pig and big are in the -ig family.

questions.q: Blend the sounds s, u, n. What is the word?
questions.explain: s-u-n makes sun.

questions.q: What is the first sound in mop?
questions.explain: Mop starts with the m sound.

questions.q: Sort the words into their families.
hints: Look at how each word ends.
Mat and sat end in a t.
Dig and wig end in i g.
questions.explain: Mat and sat are -at words. Dig and wig are -ig words.

reflect.q: What helped you read the words?

units.parent: Your child blended sounds to read words and sorted words into word families.
units.teacher: Shows letter-sound knowledge, blending CVC words and recognising -at, -ig and -un word families.
units.done: Words in a family end the same way. Change the first sound to make new words.

units.subject: English Home Language
units.title: Writing a sentence
units.caps: CAPS Grade 1 English Home Language: Writing and Language Structure (write sentences using a capital letter and a full stop)
units.intention: Today I am learning how to write a sentence properly.
units.prompt: How do you know where a sentence starts and ends?

lesson.say: A sentence tells us one whole idea. The dog runs. That is a sentence.
lesson.html:
The dog runs.

A sentence is a group of words that makes sense on its own.

lesson.say: Every sentence starts with a capital letter. A capital letter is a big letter.
lesson.html:
a → A→t → T→m → M

The cat sleeps. The first letter is a capital.

lesson.say: Most sentences end with a full stop. A full stop is a little dot that says stop.
lesson.html:
We play outside.

The full stop shows the sentence has ended.

example.q: Fix this sentence: my mum cooks.
steps: A sentence starts with a capital letter.
My mum cooks. It already ends with a full stop.

questions.q: Which one is a sentence?
hints: It starts with a capital and ends with a full stop.
questions.explain: The bird sings. It makes sense, starts with a capital and ends with a full stop.

questions.q: Which sentence is written correctly?
hints: Capital I and a full stop.
questions.explain: I like rice. has a capital letter and a full stop.

questions.q: What goes at the end of this sentence? We go to school
hints: What shows a sentence has ended?
questions.explain: We go to school. It needs a full stop.

questions.q: Put the words in order to make a sentence.
hints: Which word has a capital letter?
Which word has the full stop?
questions.explain: The sun is hot.

questions.q: Which word should start with a capital letter? the baby sleeps.
hints: The first word needs a capital.
questions.explain: The baby sleeps. The first word needs a capital.

reflect.q: What will you remember when you write?

units.parent: Your child learned that a sentence starts with a capital letter and ends with a full stop.
units.teacher: Shows understanding of sentence boundaries, capital letters and full stops, and word order.
units.done: A sentence starts with a capital letter and ends with a full stop.

units.subject: English Home Language
units.title: Story: Sipho and the Big Seed
units.caps: CAPS Grade 1 English Home Language: Listening and Speaking, Reading (listen to a story; answer questions; retell a story with a beginning, middle and end)
units.intention: Today I am listening to a story and finding its beginning, middle and end.
units.prompt: What happened in the middle of the story?
units.passage:
Sipho and the Big Seed (a 2to.iQ story)

Sipho found a big seed in the garden. "What will you grow into?" he asked.

He dug a little hole. He put the seed in the hole and covered it with soil. Then he gave it some water.

Every day, Sipho watered the seed. Every day, he looked. Nothing happened.

Then one morning, he saw a tiny green shoot. "You are growing!" Sipho shouted.

By the end of summer, a tall yellow sunflower stood in the garden. It was even taller than Sipho!

lesson.say: Listen to the story. You can press Read aloud to hear it.
lesson.html:
Sipho and the Big Seed (a 2to.iQ story)

Sipho found a big seed in the garden. "What will you grow into?" he asked.

He dug a little hole. He put the seed in the hole and covered it with soil. Then he gave it some water.

Every day, Sipho watered the seed. Every day, he looked. Nothing happened.

Then one morning, he saw a tiny green shoot. "You are growing!" Sipho shouted.

By the end of summer, a tall yellow sunflower stood in the garden. It was even taller than Sipho!

lesson.say: Every story has a beginning, a middle and an end. The beginning starts the story. The middle is what happens. The end tells how it finishes.
lesson.html:
Beginning→Middle→End

Stories go in order, like steps.

lesson.say: The people or animals in a story are the characters. Sipho is the main character.
lesson.html:
👦🌻

Sipho is the main character.

example.q: What happened at the beginning of the story?

questions.q: What did Sipho find?
questions.explain: Sipho found a big seed in the garden.

questions.q: What did Sipho give the seed every day?
questions.explain: Sipho watered the seed every day.

questions.q: How did Sipho feel when he saw the green shoot?
questions.explain: He shouted, so he was happy and excited.

questions.q: What did the seed grow into?
hints: Look at the end of the story.
questions.explain: The seed grew into a tall yellow sunflower.

questions.q: Put the story in order.
questions.explain: He found the seed, planted and watered it, and a sunflower grew.

reflect.q: How did you understand the story best?

units.parent: Your child listened to a story and told its beginning, middle and end.
units.teacher: Shows literal comprehension, inferring feelings, and sequencing a story into beginning, middle and end.
units.done: Stories have a beginning, a middle and an end.

units.subject: English Home Language
units.title: Naming words and doing words
units.caps: CAPS Grade 1 English Home Language: Language Structure and Use (nouns, verbs, pronouns I, you, he, she, it; plurals with -s)
units.intention: Today I am learning naming words and doing words.
units.prompt: How did you tell a naming word from a doing word?

lesson.say: A naming word is called a noun. It names a person, an animal, a place or a thing. Mum, dog, school and ball are nouns.
lesson.html:
Mum→dog→school→ball

Nouns name people, animals, places and things.

lesson.say: A doing word is called a verb. It tells us what someone does. Run, jump, eat and sing are verbs.
lesson.html:
🏃 🤸 🍽️ 🎤

Verbs are action words.

lesson.say: When there is more than one, we often add s. One cup, two cups.
lesson.html:
cup → cups→hat → hats→dog → dogs

Add s for more than one.

example.q: In the sentence The baby cries, which word is the doing word?
steps: Ask: what does the baby do?

questions.q: Which word is a naming word?
hints: A naming word is a thing.
questions.explain: Table is a noun. It names a thing.

questions.q: Which word is a doing word?
hints: A doing word is an action.
questions.explain: Swim is a verb. It is an action.

questions.q: One book, two …
questions.explain: One book, two books.

questions.q: Thabo kicks the ball. Which word tells what Thabo does?
questions.explain: Kicks is the doing word.

questions.q: Sort into naming words and doing words.
hints: Can you do it, or is it a thing?
questions.explain: Cat and house are nouns. Sing and eat are verbs.

options: Using the word in a sentence

units.parent: Your child learned naming words (nouns), doing words (verbs) and adding s for more than one.
units.teacher: Shows identification of nouns and verbs and regular plurals with -s.
units.done: Nouns name things. Verbs tell what we do.

units.subject: Life Skills
units.title: Healthy habits
units.caps: CAPS Grade 1 Life Skills, Beginning Knowledge and Personal and Social Well-being, Term 1: Healthy habits (sleep, healthy eating, washing hands, personal cleanliness, exercise)
units.intention: Today I am learning habits that keep my body healthy.
units.prompt: Which healthy habit will you do today?

lesson.say: Wash your hands with soap after the toilet and before you eat. Soap washes germs away.
lesson.html:
🧼 🙌 💧

Wash with soap after the toilet and before eating.

lesson.say: Fruit, vegetables and water help your body grow. Too many sweets are not good for your teeth.
lesson.html:
🍎 🥕 🥛 💧

Healthy food and water help you grow strong.

lesson.say: Children need lots of sleep every night. Playing and running every day keeps your body strong.
lesson.html:
😴 🛏️   ⚽ 🏃

Sleep and exercise are healthy habits.

example.q: Ayanda has just played in the sand. Now it is lunch time. What should she do first?
steps: She should wash her hands with soap first.

questions.q: When should you wash your hands?
hints: Germs can get on our food.
questions.explain: Wash your hands before you eat and after the toilet.

questions.q: Which snack is the healthiest?
questions.explain: A banana is fruit, so it is the healthiest.

questions.q: What is the best drink when you are thirsty?
hints: Your body needs it every day.
questions.explain: Water is the best drink.

questions.q: Sort into healthy and not healthy.
hints: Too many sweets and late nights do not.
questions.explain: Brushing teeth and playing outside are healthy.

questions.q: Why do we use soap?
questions.explain: Soap washes germs away.

reflect.q: Which healthy habit is easiest for you?

units.parent: Your child learned about washing hands, healthy food, water, sleep and exercise.
units.teacher: Shows knowledge of personal hygiene, healthy eating, sleep and exercise as healthy habits.
units.done: Healthy habits keep your body strong every day.

units.subject: Life Skills
units.title: Safe at home
units.topic: Dangers at home and emergency numbers
units.caps: CAPS Grade 1 Life Skills, Personal and Social Well-being, Term 2: Safety in the home (dangers at home; medicines and poisons; emergency numbers)
units.intention: Today I am learning how to stay safe at home and who to call for help.
units.prompt: What would you do if you saw something dangerous?

lesson.say: Some things at home can hurt us. Hot stoves, sharp knives, matches and plugs are not for playing with.
lesson.html:
🔥 🔪 🔌 🧯

Hot, sharp and electric things can hurt you. Tell a grown-up.

lesson.say: Medicine is only taken from a grown-up. Never drink from a bottle if you do not know what is inside. Some bottles have poison.
lesson.html:
💊 ☠️ 🧴

Only take medicine from a grown-up you trust.

lesson.say: In an emergency, tell a grown-up. You can call 10111 for the police and 10177 for an ambulance. From a cellphone, you can also call 112.
lesson.html:
Police 10111→Ambulance 10177→Cellphone 112

Learn your address so you can tell people where you are.

example.q: Lwazi finds a bottle with a skull on it under the sink. What should he do?
steps: Poison can make you very sick.
He should not touch it and should tell a grown-up.

questions.q: Which of these is dangerous to play with?
questions.explain: Matches can start a fire. Do not play with them.

questions.q: Who should give you medicine?
hints: Only a grown-up knows how much.
questions.explain: Only take medicine from a grown-up you trust.

questions.q: What number do you call for the police?
questions.explain: 10111 is the police number.

questions.q: Sort into safe and not safe.
items: Telling a grown-up about a danger
hints: Plugs and hot pots can hurt.
Telling a grown-up and knowing your address keep you safe.
questions.explain: Telling a grown-up and knowing your address are safe things to do.

questions.q: A pot is boiling on the stove. What should you do?
questions.explain: Stay away from hot pots and the stove.

units.parent: Your child learned about dangers at home, medicine safety and South African emergency numbers. Please practise your home address together.
units.teacher: Shows recognition of household dangers, medicine and poison safety, and emergency numbers (10111, 10177, 112).
units.done: Stay away from danger, and tell a grown-up you trust.

units.subject: Life Skills
units.title: Plants and seeds
units.topic: Plant parts and what plants need
units.caps: CAPS Grade 1 Life Skills, Beginning Knowledge, Term 3: Plants and seeds (parts of a plant; seeds; what plants need; growing a seed)
units.intention: Today I am learning the parts of a plant and what plants need to grow.
units.prompt: What would happen if a plant got no water?

lesson.say: A plant has roots, a stem, leaves and flowers. The roots are under the ground.
lesson.html:
🌸 🍃 🌱

Roots→Stem→Leaves→Flower

Roots hold the plant and drink water. The stem holds it up.

lesson.say: Plants need water, sunlight, air and soil to grow.
lesson.html:
💧 ☀️ 💨 🟫

Plants need water, sunlight, air and soil.

lesson.say: Many plants grow from seeds. A bean seed grows roots, then a shoot, then leaves.
lesson.html:
Seed→Roots→Shoot→Leaves

A seed grows into a new plant.

example.q: A plant was kept in a dark cupboard. It turned yellow. Why?
steps: The plant needs sunlight to stay green and healthy.

questions.q: Which part of the plant is under the ground?
hints: It drinks water from the soil.
questions.explain: The roots are under the ground.

questions.q: Which of these does a plant need?
questions.explain: Plants need sunlight.

questions.q: What holds the plant up?
hints: It is between the roots and the leaves.
questions.explain: The stem holds the plant up.

questions.q: Put the steps in order to grow a bean.
questions.explain: Plant it, water it, and a shoot grows.

questions.q: What do plants need?
hints: Sweets and toys are not for plants.
questions.explain: Plants need water and soil.

reflect.q: Would you like to grow a seed?

units.parent: Your child learned the parts of a plant and what plants need. You could plant a bean in a cup together.
units.teacher: Shows naming of plant parts, plant needs and the sequence of a seed germinating.
units.done: Plants need water, sunlight, air and soil to grow.

units.subject: Life Skills
units.title: Kindness and good manners
units.caps: CAPS Grade 1 Life Skills, Personal and Social Well-being, Term 3: Manners and responsibilities (greeting; taking turns; listening; sharing; kindness; honesty; respect)
units.intention: Today I am learning kind ways to treat other people.
units.prompt: How can you be kind to someone today?

lesson.say: Please, thank you and sorry are kind words. They show respect.
lesson.html:
Please→Thank you→Sorry→Excuse me

Kind words show respect.

lesson.say: When someone is speaking, we listen and wait for our turn.
lesson.html:
👂 ⏳ 🙋

Listen first, then take your turn.

lesson.say: Being honest means telling the truth, even when it is hard.
lesson.html:
✅ 🗣️

Honest people tell the truth.

example.q: You bump into a friend and their juice spills. What can you say?
steps: It was an accident, but it upset your friend.
Say sorry, and help clean up.

questions.q: A friend gives you a crayon. What do you say?
hints: Which words show you are glad?
questions.explain: We say thank you when someone helps us.

questions.q: Your teacher is talking. What should you do?
questions.explain: We listen and wait for our turn to speak.

questions.q: You broke a cup by mistake. What is the honest thing to do?
questions.explain: Telling the truth is honest.

questions.q: Sort into kind and unkind.
hints: How would the other person feel?
Sharing and saying please feel good.
questions.explain: Sharing and saying please are kind.

questions.q: How do you greet your teacher in the morning?
questions.explain: We say good morning to greet someone in the morning.

reflect.q: Which kind action will you try?

units.parent: Your child learned about kind words, listening, taking turns and being honest.
units.teacher: Shows understanding of manners, turn-taking, honesty and respectful behaviour.
units.done: Kind words and actions help everyone feel good.

units.subject: Mathematics
units.title: Number bonds to 10
units.caps: Cambridge Primary Mathematics (0096), Stage 1: Number (pairs of numbers that make 10)
units.intention: Today I am finding pairs of numbers that make 10.
units.prompt: How many fingers do you have altogether?

lesson.say: You have ten fingers. If you hold up 7 fingers, 3 are down. 7 and 3 make 10.
lesson.html:
🖐️🖐️

7 + 3 = 10

lesson.say: These pairs all make 10: 1 and 9, 2 and 8, 3 and 7, 4 and 6, 5 and 5.
lesson.html: 1 + 9→2 + 8→3 + 7→4 + 6→5 + 5

lesson.say: If 6 plus something makes 10, count on from 6 to 10: 7, 8, 9, 10. That is 4.

questions.q: Which pair makes 10?

units.parent: Your child found pairs of numbers that make 10.
units.teacher: Shows recalling number bonds to 10 and finding missing addends by counting on.

units.subject: English
units.title: Rhyming words
units.caps: Cambridge Primary English (0058), Stage 1: Reading (hearing and making rhymes)
units.intention: Today I am finding words that rhyme.
units.prompt: Do you know a song with rhyming words?

lesson.say: Words rhyme when they end with the same sound. Cat and hat rhyme. Dog and log rhyme.
lesson.html:
🐱 🎩

cat, hat

lesson.say: Say the words aloud and listen to the end. Sun, run, fun. They all end in un.
lesson.html: sun→run→fun

lesson.say: Change the first sound to make a new rhyme. From bed you can make red and fed.
lesson.html: bed → red → fed

steps: Big, dig and wig all rhyme with pig.

questions.q: Which word rhymes with 'cat'?
questions.explain: Cat and hat both end in 'at'.

questions.q: Which word rhymes with 'sun'?
questions.explain: Sun and run both end in 'un'.

questions.q: Which word rhymes with 'log'?
questions.explain: Log and frog both end in 'og'.

questions.q: Which two words rhyme?
questions.explain: Bed and red both end in 'ed'.

units.parent: Your child found and made rhyming words.
units.teacher: Shows recognising and generating rhymes by identifying shared word endings.
units.done: Rhyming words end with the same sound.

units.subject: Science
units.title: Living and not living
units.caps: Cambridge Primary Science (0097), Stage 1: Biology (sorting living and non-living things)
units.intention: Today I am sorting things into living and not living.
units.prompt: Is a tree alive? How do you know?

lesson.say: Living things grow, need food and water, and can make new living things. Plants, animals and people are living.
lesson.html: 🌳 🐕 👧

lesson.say: Things that are not living do not grow, eat or breathe. A rock, a chair and a ball are not living.
lesson.html: 🪨 🪑 ⚽

lesson.say: Some things were alive once, like a wooden table that came from a tree, or a dry leaf.
lesson.html: 🍂 🪵

example.q: Is a dog living or not living?
steps: A dog grows and can have puppies.

questions.q: Which one is living?
questions.explain: A sunflower grows and needs water.

questions.q: Which one is NOT living?
questions.explain: A car doesn't grow, eat or breathe.

questions.q: What do all living things need?
hints: Plants and animals both need it.
questions.explain: All living things need water.

questions.q: Sort them.
questions.explain: The tree and cat are living; the ball and chair are not.

units.parent: Your child sorted things into living and not living.
units.teacher: Shows identifying characteristics of living things and classifying objects.
units.done: Living things grow, need food and water, and make new living things.

units.subject: English Home Language
units.title: Saying hello
units.caps: CAPS for Learners with Severe Intellectual Disability (draft): Home Language (listening and speaking: greetings in everyday situations)
units.intention: Today I am learning to say hello and goodbye.
units.prompt: Who do you say hello to every day?

lesson.say: When we meet someone, we say hello. When we leave, we say goodbye.
lesson.html: 👋 Hello→👋 Goodbye

lesson.say: When you say hello, look at the person and smile. You can wave too.
lesson.html: 😊 👋

lesson.say: You can say: Hello, my name is. Then say your name.
lesson.html: Hello, my name is ___.

example.q: Gogo comes to visit. What do you say?

questions.q: Your teacher arrives in the morning. What do you say?
questions.explain: We say hello when we meet someone.

questions.q: Your friend is going home. What do you say?
hints: What do we say when someone leaves?
questions.explain: We say goodbye when someone leaves.

questions.q: Put it in order.
questions.explain: Look, smile, say hello.

units.parent: Your child practised greeting people: hello, goodbye and saying their name.
units.teacher: Shows using greetings in context with eye contact and gesture (functional listening and speaking).
units.done: Look, smile, and say hello.

units.subject: Life Skills
units.title: Brushing my teeth
units.caps: CAPS for Learners with Severe Intellectual Disability (draft): Life Skills (personal and social well-being: personal hygiene routines)
units.intention: Today I am learning how to brush my teeth.
units.prompt: When do you brush your teeth?

lesson.say: We brush our teeth to keep them clean and strong. We brush in the morning and at night.
lesson.html: ☀️ morning→🌙 night

lesson.say: You need a toothbrush, toothpaste and water. Use a little toothpaste, the size of a pea.
lesson.html: Toothbrush · toothpaste · 💧 water

lesson.say: Wet the brush. Put on toothpaste. Brush every tooth, front and back. Spit and rinse.
lesson.html: Wet→Toothpaste→Brush→Spit

example.q: It is bedtime. What do you do before you sleep?
steps: We brush our teeth at night.

questions.q: When do we brush our teeth?
questions.explain: We brush in the morning and at night.

questions.q: What do we brush our teeth with?
questions.explain: We use a toothbrush.

questions.q: Put the steps in order.
questions.explain: Wet, toothpaste, brush, spit and rinse.

units.parent: Your child learnt when and how to brush their teeth.
units.teacher: Shows sequencing a personal hygiene routine (personal and social well-being).
units.done: Brush in the morning and at night, every tooth.

units.subject: Mathematics
units.title: Longer and shorter
units.caps: IB PYP Mathematics: measurement (comparing and ordering lengths; non-standard units)
units.intention: Today I am comparing how long things are.
units.prompt: Who is the tallest person in your family?

lesson.say: Central idea: We compare and measure things to describe our world. Key concept: Form. Today we are inquirers.
lesson.html:
Central idea: We compare and measure things to describe our world.

Key concept: Form · Learner profile: Inquirers

lesson.say: Put two things side by side, starting at the same line. The one that goes further is longer.
lesson.html:
✏️
🖍️

The pencil is longer than the crayon.

lesson.say: We can measure with hand spans or paper clips. The table is 6 hand spans long.
lesson.html: Table: 🖐️🖐️🖐️🖐️🖐️🖐️ = 6 hand spans

example.q: A book is 4 paper clips long. A pencil is 6 paper clips long. Which is longer?

questions.q: Which is longer?
questions.explain: The snake is longer.

questions.q: Why do we line things up at the same start?
questions.explain: Starting at the same line makes the comparison fair.

questions.q: A desk is 5 hand spans. A rug is 9 hand spans. How many more hand spans is the rug?
questions.explain: 9 − 5 = 4 hand spans.

questions.q: Put them in order, shortest first.
questions.explain: Ant, cat, giraffe.

units.parent: Your child compared and measured lengths using hands and paper clips.
units.teacher: Shows comparing and ordering lengths and measuring with non-standard units (inquirer).
units.done: Line things up to compare. Count units to measure.

units.subject: Language
units.title: Beginning, middle and end
units.caps: IB PYP Language: reading and oral language (story structure: beginning, middle and end)
units.intention: Today I am finding the beginning, middle and end of a story.
units.prompt: What is your favourite story?

lesson.say: Central idea: Stories help us share ideas and feelings. Key concept: Form. Today we are communicators.
lesson.html:
Central idea: Stories help us share ideas and feelings.

Key concept: Form · Learner profile: Communicators

lesson.say: The beginning tells us who and where. The middle has a problem. The end tells us how it was solved.
lesson.html: Beginning: who and where→Middle: a problem→End: solved

lesson.say: Lindi planted a seed. The seed did not grow because there was no rain. Lindi watered it every day, and it grew into a sunflower.
lesson.html: 🌱 🌧️ 🌻

example.q: What is the problem in Lindi's story?

questions.q: How does Lindi's story begin?
questions.explain: The story begins when Lindi plants a seed.

questions.q: How does the story end?
questions.explain: It ends when the seed grows into a sunflower.

questions.q: Put the story in order.
questions.explain: Plant, problem, water, grow.

questions.q: What does the middle of a story usually have?
questions.explain: The middle usually has a problem.

units.parent: Your child found the beginning, middle and end of a story.
units.teacher: Shows identifying story structure and sequencing events (communicator).
units.done: Beginning, middle with a problem, and an end that solves it.

units.subject: Personal, Social and Physical Education
units.title: Keeping my body healthy
units.caps: IB PYP PSPE, transdisciplinary theme 'Who we are': healthy choices: food, sleep, exercise and hygiene
units.intention: Today I am finding out what my body needs to be healthy.
units.prompt: What do you do to feel strong and well?

lesson.say: Our theme is Who we are. Central idea: The choices we make help our bodies stay healthy. Key concept: Responsibility. Today we are balanced.
lesson.html:
Central idea: The choices we make help our bodies stay healthy.

Key concept: Responsibility · Learner profile: Balanced

lesson.say: My body needs healthy food, water, sleep and exercise to grow strong.
lesson.html: 🍎 💧 😴 🏃

lesson.say: Playing outside, eating fruit and vegetables, and washing my hands help me stay healthy.
lesson.html: Play→Eat well→Wash hands→Sleep

example.q: Is an apple or a packet of sweets a healthier snack?
steps: An apple has vitamins and fibre.

questions.q: Which is a healthy snack?
questions.explain: Fruit is a healthy snack.

questions.q: What does your body need every night?
questions.explain: Sleep helps your body grow and rest.

questions.q: Which keeps your body strong?
questions.explain: Exercise keeps you strong.

questions.q: What should you drink most?
questions.explain: Water is the best drink.

units.parent: Your child explored food, sleep and exercise choices that keep them healthy.
units.teacher: Who we are: shows identifying healthy choices and taking responsibility for wellbeing (balanced).
units.done: Healthy food, water, sleep and play keep me strong.
